issues.title: Node execution started before being enqueued and marked as TAKEN
issues.description: The `start_execution` method is called before `enqueue_node`, which violates the expected state machine flow. The node is added to the `_executing_nodes` set before it's marked as TAKEN or added to the ready queue. This creates a race condition where concurrent operations might observe a node in the executing state while it's still in UNKNOWN state, leading to inconsistent state validation failures. The correct order should be: first enqueue (which marks as TAKEN and adds to queue), then start execution tracking.

issues.title: Edge marked as skipped after recursive propagation breaks skip chain
issues.description: In `_propagate_skip_to_node`, the edge is marked as skipped AFTER the recursive call to `propagate_skip_from_edge`. During the recursive propagation, the edge state is still UNKNOWN rather than SKIPPED. The `propagate_skip_from_edge` method analyzes incoming edge states and stops processing if any edge is UNKNOWN (line 56). This causes the skip propagation to terminate prematurely, leaving downstream nodes in an incorrect state instead of properly propagating the skip status through the entire dependency chain.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30251 - fix: workflow incorrectly marked as completed while nodes are still executing

structured_output.summary:
The PR fixes a premature exit of the graph dispatcher loop. When a downstream node becomes ready through skip propagation (its last incoming edge is skipped and another incoming edge is taken), `SkipPropagator.propagate_skip_from_edge` only called `enqueue_node`. That left the node out of `_executing_nodes`, so once the ready queue drained, `is_execution_complete()` returned true while the node was still pending. The fix adds `start_execution` next to `enqueue_node`, which matches the pairing already used in `event_handlers.py` for normal node completion. It also adds a new unit-test module for `SkipPropagator`.

The enqueue-plus-start fix is correct and I'd keep it. However, the diff also reorders two lines in `_propagate_skip_to_node`, moving `mark_edge_skipped` after the recursive `propagate_skip_from_edge` call. I ran the real `GraphStateManager` and `SkipPropagator` logic on a three-node chain (skipped A → B → C). With the base ordering both B and C end up SKIPPED. With the PR's ordering only the first edge is marked, and B and C stay UNKNOWN. The reason: `propagate_skip_from_edge` checks the real states of the downstream node's incoming edges, and the edge being propagated is still UNKNOWN at that point, so the recursion always returns early. Any skip chain of length two or more is now broken. The new unit tests cannot catch this because they mock `analyze_edge_states`, so the ordering is never exercised. A stray debug `print` is also left in the fix.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The enqueue/start_execution fix is the right idea, but the PR as written introduces a regression. Reordering `mark_edge_skipped` after the recursive propagation stops skip cascades after the first hop. Downstream nodes in any skip chain of length two or more remain UNKNOWN and never get skipped, which is a core-workflow correctness bug. The tests pass only because they mock the state analysis. Fix the ordering, remove the debug print, and add a test that runs real state through a multi-hop chain.

architecture.overview:
The graph engine (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine`) runs nodes through a ready queue. `GraphStateManager` tracks node and edge states (UNKNOWN/TAKEN/SKIPPED) and the set of executing nodes. A dispatcher loop exits once `is_execution_complete()` is true, meaning the ready queue is empty and no node is executing. When a branch node finishes, `EdgeProcessor.handle_branch_completion` calls `SkipPropagator.skip_branch_paths` for unselected edges. The propagator walks downstream and either enqueues a node whose incoming edges include a taken one, or marks the node and its outgoing edges as skipped and recurses.

The PR changes the propagator in two ways. First, when a node is enqueued from the skip path it is also registered as executing, so it counts toward completion. This matches how `event_handlers.py` pairs `enqueue_node` with `start_execution` for normal completion. Second, it reorders the edge marking so edges are marked skipped after recursion. That reorder breaks the recursive analysis, because the edge being propagated still reads UNKNOWN when its downstream node is checked.
steps: Entry point: a branch node completes in `EventHandler` (`event_handlers.py`). `EdgeProcessor.handle_branch_completion` categorizes its outgoing edges and passes the unselected ones to `SkipPropagator.skip_branch_paths`.

Skip path: `skip_branch_paths` marks each unselected edge SKIPPED and calls `propagate_skip_from_edge`. That method inspects the downstream node's incoming edges via `GraphStateManager.analyze_edge_states`, which returns has_unknown, has_taken, or all_skipped.

Changed branch (has_taken): the PR adds `start_execution(downstream)` before `enqueue_node(downstream)`. This keeps the node in `_executing_nodes` while it sits in the ready queue, so `is_execution_complete()` stays false until it runs. A debug `print` was also added here.

Changed branch (all_skipped): `_propagate_skip_to_node` marks the node SKIPPED and walks its outgoing edges. The PR moves `mark_edge_skipped` after `propagate_skip_from_edge`. Because the propagation reads live edge states, the current edge must already be SKIPPED before recursion, so this reorder stops the cascade after one hop.

Verification gap: the new tests in `test_skip_propagator.py` mock `GraphStateManager`, so `analyze_edge_states` returns canned dicts and the edge-state ordering is never exercised. A chain test against the real state manager is needed.

findings.title: Reordered mark_edge_skipped breaks skip cascade beyond one hop
findings.body:
Moving `mark_edge_skipped` after `propagate_skip_from_edge` in `_propagate_skip_to_node` breaks recursion. `propagate_skip_from_edge` reads the live states of the downstream node's incoming edges. At the moment it runs, the edge being propagated is still UNKNOWN, so `analyze_edge_states` reports `has_unknown=True` and the call returns immediately. The downstream node is never marked SKIPPED.

I checked this by running the real `GraphStateManager` and `SkipPropagator` source (with the Flask-dependent package imports stubbed) on a chain A(skipped) → B → C. With the base ordering, B and C both end SKIPPED. With the PR ordering, only e1 is SKIPPED, while B and C remain UNKNOWN.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py" lines="81-87"}

::callout{type="warning"}
Any workflow where a skipped node feeds another node that depends only on skipped paths will leave that downstream node UNKNOWN. This is the same class of scenario the PR claims to fix, so it's a regression, not just an untested edge.

Restore the base order: mark the edge SKIPPED first, then recurse.

::suggestion{file="api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py" lines="84-87"}
            # Mark edge skipped before recursing so downstream analysis sees it
            self._state_manager.mark_edge_skipped(edge.id)
            # Recursively propagate skip
            self.propagate_skip_from_edge(edge.id)
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py`, `_propagate_skip_to_node` (around lines 81-87) calls `propagate_skip_from_edge(edge.id)` before `mark_edge_skipped(edge.id)`. Because propagation reads live edge states and the edge is still UNKNOWN, the recursion returns early and multi-hop skip chains never complete. Swap the two calls so the edge is marked SKIPPED before recursing, matching the ordering in `skip_branch_paths` (around lines 96-97). Keep the `start_execution` + `enqueue_node` change in `propagate_skip_from_edge` as is. Then add a test that drives real `GraphStateManager` state through a multi-node skip chain, not mocked `analyze_edge_states`.

findings.title: Unit tests mock the state analysis, so they cannot detect the ordering regression
findings.body:
The new tests in `test_skip_propagator.py` replace `GraphStateManager` with `create_autospec` and set `analyze_edge_states.return_value` to canned dicts. Edge states are never read, so the order of `mark_edge_skipped` relative to recursion cannot change any result. The chain test `test_propagate_skip_from_edge_recursively_propagates_through_graph` (around line 186) passes because of its own canned `all_skipped=True`, not because the propagation logic works.

The test in `test_propagate_skip_to_node_marks_node_and_outgoing_edges_skipped` (line 115) also admits it can't check recursion ("We'll trust the logic"). Its assertions only check `mark_edge_skipped` calls, so they would pass with the regressed ordering too. Since the failing case is ordering-dependent, a mock-only test gives false confidence.

::callout{type="warning"}
These tests assert on internal calls, not observable outcomes. For skip propagation, the outcome is each node's and edge's state after the call.

Add tests that use a real `GraphStateManager` with a small real or stub graph, and assert final node and edge states for: a two-hop skip chain, a join where one incoming edge is taken (node enqueued and in `get_executing_nodes()`), and a join with an unknown edge (no change). Keep the mock-based tests only where the call contract itself matters.
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/test_skip_propagator.py`, the tests mock `GraphStateManager` and fix `analyze_edge_states` to canned values, so they can't detect edge-ordering bugs in `SkipPropagator._propagate_skip_to_node` (`skip_propagator.py`). Add tests that use a real `GraphStateManager` (with a simple in-memory ready queue) over a small graph and assert final node and edge states: (1) a chain skipped A→B→C ends with B and C SKIPPED, (2) a join node with one taken incoming edge is enqueued and appears in `get_executing_nodes()`, (3) a join with an unknown incoming edge is left untouched. Replace the 'We'll trust the logic' assertion in `test_propagate_skip_to_node_marks_node_and_outgoing_edges_skipped` with state-based assertions. Follow the existing test style (Arrange/Act/Assert docstrings).

findings.title: Leftover debug print in production skip path
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py`, remove the debug `print(f"Starting execution for node: ...")` line (around line 62) in `propagate_skip_from_edge`. Keep the `self._state_manager.start_execution(downstream_node_id)` and `enqueue_node` calls directly after the comment. Do not replace it with another print.

findings.title: Starting execution where the node is enqueued fixes the stuck dispatcher
findings.body: Adding `start_execution` next to `enqueue_node` in the has_taken branch matches the pairing the event handlers already use (`event_handlers.py`, around lines 196-197 and 279-280). A node in the ready queue is now always tracked in `_executing_nodes` until its success, failure, or pause handler calls `finish_execution`. That means `is_execution_complete()` can't report done while a skip-activated node is still pending, which is the reported bug.
